articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 with Persistent Memory and Extended Reasoning Chains
articles.summary: OpenAI officially released GPT-5, featuring a native long-term memory architecture that retains context across sessions and significantly improved multi-step reasoning capabilities. Benchmarks show a 38% improvement on graduate-level STEM tasks compared to GPT-4o, with notably reduced hallucination rates on factual queries. The model also introduces a new "deep research" mode that can autonomously browse, synthesize, and cite sources over extended workflows.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves New State-of-the-Art on Multimodal Scientific Reasoning
articles.summary: DeepMind unveiled Gemini Ultra 2, which sets new records on multimodal benchmarks requiring joint interpretation of images, charts, code, and natural language. The model demonstrates near-expert-level performance in interpreting medical imaging and molecular structure prediction when paired with specialized tool-use agents. Google is integrating the model across Workspace, Cloud, and a revamped AI-powered Search experience rolling out globally.

articles.title: Figure Robotics Demonstrates Fully Autonomous Warehouse Shift with Figure 02 Humanoids
articles.summary: Figure completed a milestone 8-hour autonomous warehouse shift at a BMW logistics facility, with a team of Figure 02 humanoid robots performing picking, packing, and palletizing without human intervention. The robots used on-device vision-language models for real-time task adaptation and demonstrated a 99.2% successful grasp rate across heterogeneous objects. This marks a significant step toward commercial-scale deployment of general-purpose humanoid labor.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Enters Limited Production, Promises Sub-$25K Price Point by 2028
articles.summary: Tesla announced that its Optimus Gen 3 humanoid robot has entered limited production at its Texas Gigafactory, with initial units deployed internally for manufacturing tasks. The new generation features 28 degrees of freedom in its hands, improved battery life of 14 hours under moderate workload, and a significantly revamped neural network stack for whole-body control. Musk reiterated a target retail price under $25,000 once full-scale production is achieved.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Claude 'Opus 4' with Constitutional-AI-Driven Agentic Capabilities
articles.summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4, its most capable model to date, featuring advanced agentic workflows governed by a refined Constitutional AI framework designed to maintain alignment during multi-step autonomous tasks. The model can execute complex software engineering tasks end-to-end, including writing, testing, and deploying code across repositories with minimal human oversight. Early enterprise adopters report up to 60% reduction in time spent on routine engineering and data analysis workflows.

articles.title: ASML Ships First Production High-NA EUV Scanner to Intel's Ohio Fab
articles.summary: ASML confirmed delivery of its first full-production TWINSCAN EXE:5000 high-numerical-aperture EUV lithography system to Intel's new Ohio fabrication facility, enabling sub-2nm patterning. The system achieves 0.55 NA optics with an overlay accuracy below 1nm, a critical enabler for next-generation chip architectures. This shipment represents a pivotal moment in the semiconductor industry's roadmap toward angstrom-scale transistor manufacturing.

articles.title: Neuralink Receives FDA Approval for Expanded Brain-Computer Interface Trials in Paralysis Patients
articles.summary: The FDA granted Neuralink approval to expand its PRIME clinical trial to 50 additional patients with spinal cord injuries and ALS, following positive 18-month outcomes from its initial cohort. Participants demonstrated sustained high-bandwidth cursor and robotic arm control at over 100 bits per second, with no serious device-related adverse events reported. The expanded trial will also test a next-generation implant with twice the electrode count for finer motor decoding.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics and Hyundai Unveil Atlas Electric for Commercial Construction Tasks
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics, in partnership with parent company Hyundai, officially announced the commercial availability of its fully electric Atlas humanoid robot tailored for construction environments. The robot can carry loads up to 35 kg, navigate unstructured terrain including scaffolding and stairs, and perform supervised drilling and fastening tasks using standard power tools. The companies are targeting pilot deployments with three major construction firms in South Korea and the United States by Q4 2026.
